description: Detail-page mobile adaptation: bottom floating primary-action bar, bottom-sliding destructive-action confirmation drawer, read-only narrow status-header tier, and pinned reference-rail narrow collapse.

Refactor the existing desktop RuntimeDecisionSurface to consume both helpers so desktop and the upcoming narrow surface cannot diverge. runtime-action-handlers.ts exports invokeAction(kind, { decision, mutations }) mapping every action kind to the correct mutation.mutate(...) payload, including the stopRecoverable ? forceStop : stop split and send-back's { stage: decision.approvalStage, body }

Existing RuntimeDecisionSurface.test.tsx scenarios pass unchanged: recoverable stop copy, irreversible stop copy, send-back form submission, and every primary action (start/approve/stop/retry/resume/rerun)

tasks.title: Build the narrow action surface: MobileActionBar + ConfirmationDrawer + page-level split + padding
tasks.spec: specs/issue-detail-mobile-action-bar/spec.md#Single Primary Action Surfaced in a Bottom Floating Bar
tasks.description: Add MobileActionBar.tsx and ConfirmationDrawer.tsx under pages/issue-detail/ui/. In IssueDetailPage.tsx apply the page-level conditional split (design D1): on narrow (<lg) do NOT render RuntimeDecisionSurface in the header tier, render MobileActionBar instead; at lg+ keep RuntimeDecisionSurface in the header tier unchanged. MobileActionBar renders the single decision.primary button, owns confirmKind state, and renders ConfirmationDrawer for destructive (stop/send-back) confirmation. Wire CSS offsets keyed on md (design D5) and scroll-container bottom padding conditional on the bar (design D6).
acceptanceCriteria: On narrow viewports IssueDetailPage does not render RuntimeDecisionSurface in the status-header tier and renders MobileActionBar with the single decision.primary control (start/stop/approve/send-back/retry/resume/rerun) sourced from deriveRuntimeDecision via the T-001 invokeAction helper
MobileActionBar renders only when decision.primary is non-null; it does not render and reserves no space for done/archived/no-primary runtime summaries

Bar is fixed to the bottom, sits above MobileBottomNav when the nav is present (below md), and anchors flush to the bottom edge in the 768-1024px band with no nav space reserved (CSS keyed on md, design D5)

The detail page scroll container reserves bottom padding only when the bar is present (isNarrowViewport && decision.primary) so the last comment is never obscured; nav-only padding still applies when no primary action exists

Stop and send-back on narrow open a bottom-sliding ConfirmationDrawer (fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0, translate-y slide via tw-animate-css, role='dialog', aria-modal='true', Esc-to-close, focus moves to drawer on open); no centered/full-screen dialog and no inline confirmation block renders on narrow

Drawer consequence copy is sourced from getStopConsequenceCopy: recoverable stop states progress is preserved/resumable, irreversible stop states it cannot be resumed; send-back drawer includes the feedback Textarea plus Confirm and Cancel controls wired to the existing mutations via invokeAction
The sticky StatusHeadline (z-20) remains visible and uncovered while the ConfirmationDrawer (z-50, bottom-anchored, content-sized) is open

At lg+ (1024px and wider) the desktop layout is fully restored: RuntimeDecisionSurface renders in the status-header tier with inline confirmation and neither MobileActionBar nor ConfirmationDrawer renders in the DOM
A narrow x runtime-summary test matrix passes for both layouts: approval (approve), failed/blocked, queued/backlog (start), running (stop), done (no bar), and archived
An explicit spec test at ~900px asserts flush-bottom bar anchorage with no reserved nav space (the 768-1024px band)
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/issue-detail/ui/MobileActionBar.tsx, ConfirmationDrawer.tsx, updated IssueDetailPage.tsx; narrow/desktop spec-test matrix green
tasks.notes: Covers capabilities issue-detail-mobile-action-bar, issue-detail-confirmation-drawer, and the narrow-viewport split portion of issue-detail-status-header. z-index layering per design D4: StatusHeadline z-20, MobileActionBar z-30, ConfirmationDrawer z-50, global nav/FAB z-40. No dimming scrim that would cover the headline (design D3).

tasks.title: Pin the reference-rail narrow collapse invariant and ordering
tasks.spec: specs/issue-detail-reference-rail/spec.md#Narrow-Screen Collapse Into Stacked Expandable Sections After the Reading Flow
tasks.description: Audit the reference-rail document order to confirm every rail section renders after the last reading-flow item on narrow viewports, fixing the ordering if the audit finds otherwise (design D7, mostly delivered by #341). Lock the invariant with tests: desktop right column at lg+, narrow stacked CollapsibleRailCard sections, low-frequency drift/convergence collapsed by default on every viewport, rail contents exclusivity, and lightest visual weight.
acceptanceCriteria: A document-order audit confirms (and corrects if needed) that every reference-rail section is positioned after the last reading-flow item on narrow viewports
At lg+ the rail renders as a right column beside the reading flow and is narrower than the reading-flow column, with no mobile-only element (floating bar or drawer) rendering
On narrow viewports the rail renders as stacked CollapsibleRailCard sections (no right column) following the reading flow
Drift and convergence panels are collapsed by default on every viewport and expand only on a deliberate user action

The rail holds only metadata/configuration/non-runtime actions (details, model, workflow-profile, prerequisites, non-runtime IssueActionsCard, drift, convergence) and excludes the runtime decision surface, progress/outputs, changes/diff, commits, description, and comments
The reference rail carries the lightest visual weight of the three detail-page tiers
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes
tasks.output: Reference-rail ordering audit + any structural fix in IssueDetailPage.tsx/cards; rail-collapse invariant tests green
tasks.notes: Independent of the action-surface relocation (#341 already delivered the collapse via forceCollapsed on CollapsibleRailCard).
